subject: Post-call: SKU & unit economics + batch window assumptions
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Post-call: SKU & unit economics + batch window assumptions

Hi Olivia / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap + asks so we can size an accurate price estimate and a small POC: 

1) Token volumes: rough monthly range you shared was 10M – 60M tokens (peak month). Can you confirm whether that 60M is a sustained month or a 1–2 day spike tied to marketing events?

2) Target unit price: you mentioned a target of ~$12k / 1M tokens for the initial phase (is that $/1M inbound tokens, outbound, or both?). Clarify whether that target is for raw token count or after batching/compaction.

3) Batching & concurrency assumptions: we want to validate continuous-batching expectations. From the call I captured: short requests (~200 tokens) dominated, 60% prefix reuse, 3 second median inter-request gap per user, and an expectation that the front-end will allow 150ms of batching delay to improve throughput. Is that accurate? If not, please correct.

Next steps I propose: 
- Olivia/Tom: send a 1-week sample of traffic (CSV stub is fine) with timestamps and approximate token counts so we can run a replay and produce a cost projection.
- Marissa: I’ll ask you to run a quick sensitivity analysis against 2 batching windows (50ms, 150ms) and 2 concurrency targets (16, 64) and return estimated $/1M tokens.
- Laura / Aditya: if we need to recommend quantization or model variant tradeoffs for cost parity, please flag the minimal R&D effort.

I attached a tiny sample CSV template (finx_token_sample.csv) and a 1-page draft of our batching assumptions.

Appreciate a quick confirmation on the three bullets above so we can lock a proposal by EOD Wednesday.

— Marcus

Marcus —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Volume: the 60M is a spike month tied to our End-of-Quarter reporting push — typically we expect 18–24M/month steady state. The 60M was a 4–5 day concentrated window.

2) Target price: when I said ~$12k / 1M I meant the blended $/1M for total tokens consumed (in + out combined) that we can budget against. We understand this will vary with batching.

3) Batching: front-end team is comfortable with up to 200ms at the proxy layer, but we’d prefer to see latency impact estimates. Median inter-request gap is closer to 2.5s across our sample users; some heavy traders burst at sub-second. Prefix reuse is high for alert templates (~70%), but free-form queries are ~30%.

I’ll have Tom deliver a 7-day sample by end of day tomorrow (has scrubbed PII). Attaching a note on our sample format.

Best,
Olivia

Thanks team — I ran a small replay against an internal synthetic set while we wait for FinX's sample. High level findings attached; key takeaways below.

Summary (synthetic baseline approximating FinX profile):
- Workload: 70% short requests (~150 tokens total), 30% free-form (avg 450 tokens).
- Prefix reuse: 60–70% on templates; replay modeled 65%.

Scenarios (cost shown as $/1M tokens - blended in+out):
- No batching, concurrency 16: $21,300 per 1M tokens; p95 latency 490ms.
- 50ms batching window, concurrency 16: $15,900 per 1M tokens; p95 latency 560ms (median +40ms).
- 150ms batching window, concurrency 64: $11,600 per 1M tokens; p95 latency 710ms (median +85ms).

Notes: 
- Continuous batching (150ms) yields the best unit economics but increases p95 notably for the small subset (<10%) of sub-second burst users.
- Quantization (int8) can save ~10% on cost; moving to int4 adds another ~20% but requires model validation for hallucination risk.
- If FinX can accept a hybrid policy (150ms on non-interactive routes, 50ms on interactive), we can hit the $12k target blended across traffic.

Attachments: batching-sensitivity-finx-v1.csv (breakdown), batching-assumptions-v1.pdf (annotated)

I’ll re-run once we get their real sample and include a simple quickstart config for Dedicated pool sizing.

— Marissa
